The terrifying reality of being a Roman 'Urinaris' (urine collector) in 1st-century Rome, who had to survive the toxic, explosive fumes of the city's massive public vats to secure the empire's most valuable cleaning agent.

The desperate 48 hours of a Mayan royal midwife in Tikal during a lunar eclipse, forced to perform bloodletting rituals under threat of execution to protect an unborn heir from the 'bite' of the jaguar moon.
The sudden, catastrophic ruin of a wealthy Pompeian baker named Terentius Neo on the morning of Vesuvius's eruption, as he chose to stay behind to lock up his prized grain vaults rather than flee.

The harrowing journey of a Persian 'Chapar Khaneh' royal mail courier who had to ride through a blinding sandstorm in the Zagros Mountains to deliver a message of impending rebellion, knowing failure meant execution.
The high-stakes survival story of a Greek 'Katadotes' (professional diver) hired by the Athenian navy to sabotage Persian warship anchor ropes in the pitch-black, freezing depths of the Aegean Sea.

The brutal night of a Mayan 'Chilam' (jaguar priest) in Palenque forced to ingest a toxic, hallucinating enema of fermented balché and toad venom to channel a war prophecy, knowing a wrong prediction meant being sacrificed to the underworld.

The terrifying dawn of an Egyptian 'Web-priest' inside the dark, suffocating tomb of Ramesses III, who realized he had accidentally broken a sacred protective clay seal—an offense punishable by being impaled alive to prevent the pharaoh’s soul from being eaten by demons.
